title: Practice 4: Accusative endings: nouns, adjectives, pronouns

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.prompt: Catherine wanted to go to the shopping center.
exercises.why: So, masculine nouns denoting inanimate objects in the accusative case are the same as in the nominative case. If they're animated nouns, they follow the genitive rules, which are: add **-а**, and replace **-й** and **-ь** with **-я**. Neuter nouns, regardless of animation, also keep their nominative forms in the accusative case. Feminine words are the only words to have their own accusative ending: **-а** becomes **-у**, and **-я** becomes **-ю**. Feminine nouns ending in the soft sign **-ь** do not change. — From the Wikibooks Russian textbook (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 46.
exercises.context: So, masculine nouns denoting inanimate objects in the accusative case are the same as in the nominative case. (From the Wikibooks Russian textbook (CC BY-SA 4.0))
